headline: A Game Boy survived a bombing and still worked.
slides: Army medic Stephan Scoggins had a Game Boy with him in the Gulf War.
His barracks were bombed. The case was scorched and the buttons half-melted.
It still turned on and played Tetris.
Nintendo sent him a new one 'as a special Desert Storm courtesy.'
The burnt one played Tetris on loop in Nintendo's New York store for years.
It was retired from display and went back to Nintendo's offices in Redmond.
sources: Sources: Military.com, The Star (2025 fact check), Nintendo Life, GameSpot (2023)
caption:
they don't make them like this any more. literally
